attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	# MCP Server
2	
3	This package serves an [OpenAPI](https://www.openapis.org/)-driven
4	[Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) (MCP) endpoint at
5	`/mcp`. It exposes a curated, memo-focused toolset over the **Streamable HTTP**
6	transport using the official `github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk`.
7	
8	The core design principle: **tool calls execute in-process against the existing
9	REST API.** The package owns no store or service logic of its own. Each tool is
10	derived from an operation in the generated OpenAPI document
11	(`proto/gen/openapi.yaml`, embedded via `proto.OpenAPIYAML()`), and a tool call
12	is translated into the matching `/api/v1/...` HTTP request and run against the
13	same Echo server that serves the public API. This keeps OpenAPI as the single
14	source of truth and reuses the API's authentication and authorization as-is.
15	
16	## Integration
17	
18	`server.NewServer` calls `mcp.NewMCPService` after registering the API, file, RSS, and gRPC-gateway routes, passing the same Echo server:
19	
20	```go
21	mcpService, err := mcp.NewMCPService(profile, echoServer)
22	if err != nil {
23	    return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to create MCP service")
24	}
25	mcpService.RegisterRoutes(echoServer)
26	```
27	
28	The service advertises the **tools** capability only — no prompts, no resources.
29	
30	## Startup flow
31	
32	`NewMCPService` (`service.go`) wires everything up at construction time and fails
33	fast on any inconsistency:
34	
35	1. `loadMCPServiceOpenAPISpec` parses the embedded `proto.OpenAPIYAML()` bytes
36	   into an `openAPISpec`.
37	2. `buildOperationRegistry` (`openapi.go`) indexes every operation by
38	   `operationId`, recording method, path, resolved request-body schema, and
39	   resolved 200 response schema.
40	3. `buildCuratedTools` (`catalog.go`) selects the allowlisted operation IDs and
41	   converts each into an `*sdkmcp.Tool` plus a `registeredOperation`. Missing
42	   IDs or duplicate tool names are construction errors.
43	4. Each tool is registered with `server.AddTool(tool, newMCPToolHandler(...))`.
44	5. `sdkmcp.NewStreamableHTTPHandler` wraps the server in stateless,
45	   JSON-response mode (no SSE, no session tracking).
46	
47	## Request flow
48	
49	`RegisterRoutes` binds `echoServer.Any("/mcp", ...)`. Each request:
50	
51	1. `isAllowedMCPOrigin` (`origin.go`) rejects disallowed cross-origin browser requests with `403`.
52	2. The SDK streamable handler dispatches the MCP message.
53	3. On a `tools/call` request, `newMCPToolHandler` (`service.go`) decodes the JSON
54	   arguments into a map.
55	4. `validateToolArguments` (`validation.go`) checks them against the tool's
56	   input schema.
57	5. The caller's `Authorization` header is read from the request (`request.Extra.Header` on the SDK's `*sdkmcp.CallToolRequest`).
58	6. `apiAdapter.execute` (`adapter.go`) builds the API request
59	   (`buildAPIRequest`: path-parameter substitution, query encoding, JSON body),
60	   forwards the bearer token, and runs it against the Echo server through an
61	   `httptest.ResponseRecorder`.
62	7. The recorder body is decoded; a non-2xx status becomes a tool error
63	   (`newToolErrorResult`), otherwise the value is wrapped by
64	   `newStructuredToolResult`.
65	
66	## Schema resolution
67	
68	MCP tool schemas must be self-contained JSON Schema, but the OpenAPI components
69	use `$ref`. `openapi.go` resolves these into local definitions:
70	
71	- **Top-level inlining.** The request-body and 200-response schemas for an
72	  operation are resolved with `inlineRef = true`, so the outermost `$ref` is
73	  expanded in place (`resolveSchemaRef` → `resolveSchemaValue` → `resolveSchemaMap`).
74	- **Nested refs become `$defs`.** Any `$ref` encountered below the top level is
75	  rewritten to a local `#/$defs/<Name>` pointer, and the referenced component is
76	  collected into a `$defs` map (`addSchemaDef`).
77	- **Cycle safety.** Recursive component schemas are handled by seeding
78	  `defs[name]` with a placeholder and tracking `resolving[name]` before
79	  recursing, so a schema that references itself terminates
80	  (`addSchemaDef`).
81	
82	`catalog.go` then assembles the per-tool input schema in
83	`inputSchemaForOperation`:
84	
85	- Path and query parameters become top-level properties; any required
86	  parameter stays in `required`.
87	- A request body becomes a single `body` property; a required body adds `body`
88	  to `required`. Body `$defs` are lifted to the schema's top-level `$defs`.
89	- The schema sets `"additionalProperties": false`.
90	
91	The output schema is the operation's 200 `application/json` schema. When a 200
92	response has no JSON body, the fallback is:
93	
94	```json
95	{ "type": "object", "properties": { "ok": { "type": "boolean" } } }
96	```
97	
98	## Endpoint, transport & auth
99	
100	- **Endpoint:** `POST /mcp` (the SDK may also use `GET`/`DELETE` on the same
101	  path for the Streamable HTTP transport).
102	- **Transport:** Streamable HTTP, **stateless**, JSON responses.
103	- **Auth:** the caller's `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header is forwarded to
104	  the in-process API request. Mutating tools therefore require a valid token
105	  (personal access token or access token); public reads may work without one,
106	  exactly as the REST API allows.
107	- **Origin safety:** `isAllowedMCPOrigin` allows a request when the `Origin`
108	  header is absent (desktop clients commonly omit it), when its host matches
109	  the request `Host` header (host comparison only — scheme is not checked), or
110	  when it matches the configured `profile.InstanceURL`. Anything else gets
111	  `403`. This guards against DNS-rebinding from browsers.
112	
113	### Connecting a client
114	
115	Point any Streamable HTTP MCP client at `https://<your-instance>/mcp` and supply
116	a personal access token as a bearer credential. Example client config:
117	
118	```json
119	{
120	  "mcpServers": {
121	    "memos": {
122	      "type": "http",
123	      "url": "https://<your-instance>/mcp",
124	      "headers": {
125	        "Authorization": "Bearer <your-personal-access-token>"
126	      }
127	    }
128	  }
129	}
130	```
131	
132	## Tool surface
133	
134	The server exposes a curated allowlist (`curatedOperationIDs` in `catalog.go`),
135	centered on memos and attachments, plus two read-only orientation tools:
136	`shortcut_list_shortcuts` (surfaces a user's saved CEL filters for reuse with
137	`memo_list_memos`) and `auth_get_current_user` (a "whoami" so an agent can
138	resolve its own user — the single allowed auth/identity operation):
139	
140	| OpenAPI operation | MCP tool |
141	| --- | --- |
142	| `MemoService_ListMemos` | `memo_list_memos` |

162	
163	**Naming rule** (`toolNameFromOperationID`): drop the `Service` suffix from the
164	subject and convert both subject and method from camelCase to snake_case, joined
165	by `_`. So `MemoService_ListMemos → memo_list_memos`.
166	
167	**Annotations** (`annotationsForOperation`) start from the HTTP method:
168	
169	| Method | ReadOnly | Destructive | Idempotent |
170	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
171	| GET | true | false | true |
172	| DELETE | false | true | true |
173	| other (POST, PATCH, …) | false | false | false |
174	
175	A per-operation override (`idempotentOperationIDs`) then corrects cases the
176	method heuristic gets wrong: `MemoService_SetMemoAttachments` and
177	`MemoService_SetMemoRelations` are PATCH but declaratively replace the full set
178	on a memo, so they report `IdempotentHint: true`.
179	
180	`OpenWorldHint` is `false` for all tools. Annotations are client hints; they do
181	not replace API authorization.
182	
183	**Result shape.** Every result carries object-shaped `structuredContent`
184	(`normalizeStructuredContent` in `result.go`):
185	
186	- a JSON object is returned unchanged;
187	- an empty response becomes `{ "ok": true }`;
188	- a bare array becomes `{ "result": [...] }`;
189	- a scalar becomes `{ "result": value }`.
190	
191	This is deliberate: it fixes [#6022](https://github.com/usememos/memos/issues/6022),
192	where collection tools returned a bare array that strict MCP clients reject.
193	
194	## Error handling
195	
196	Failures are returned as MCP tool errors (`CallToolResult` with `IsError: true`
197	and an `error.message` in `structuredContent`), not JSON-RPC protocol errors —
198	the handler returns `(result, nil)`:
199	
200	| Failure | Result |
201	| --- | --- |
202	| Arguments are not valid JSON | tool error: decode message |
203	| Arguments fail schema validation | tool error: validation message |
204	| Missing required path parameter | tool error: `missing required path parameter "..."` |
205	| Missing required request body | tool error: `missing required request body "body"` |
206	| API responds non-2xx | tool error: `"<code> <reason phrase>: <api message>"` (e.g. `"404 Not Found: ..."`) (`apiErrorMessage`) |
207	| API response body is not decodable JSON | tool error: decode message |
208	
209	## Core files
210	
211	| File | Responsibility |
212	| --- | --- |
213	| `service.go` | Constructs the MCP server, registers tools, builds the streamable HTTP handler, and binds the `/mcp` route. |
214	| `catalog.go` | The curated operation allowlist, tool naming, input/output schema assembly, and method-derived annotations. |
215	| `adapter.go` | Translates a tool call into an `/api/v1/...` request and runs it in-process against the Echo server. |
216	| `openapi.go` | Parses the OpenAPI spec, builds the operation registry, and resolves `$ref` schemas into self-contained JSON Schema. |
217	| `validation.go` | Validates tool-call arguments against the tool's input schema. |
218	| `origin.go` | `Origin`-header check for browser DNS-rebinding safety. |
219	| `result.go` | Normalizes API responses into object-shaped `structuredContent` and builds error results. |
220	
221	## Adding a tool
222	
223	1. Add the OpenAPI `operationId` to `curatedOperationIDs` in `catalog.go`.
224	2. If the operation is **not** in the generated OpenAPI, add or adjust the
225	   proto/API surface first, then regenerate:
226	
227	   ```bash
228	   cd proto && buf generate
229	   ```
230	
231	3. Extend the tests in `catalog_test.go` / `service_test.go` to cover the new
232	   tool.
233	
234	Never hand-edit `proto/gen/openapi.yaml` or other generated output — change the
235	proto definitions and regenerate.
236	
237	## Testing
238	
239	```bash
240	go test ./server/router/mcp/...
241	```
242	
243	- `openapi_test.go` — spec parsing, registry building, `$ref` resolution.
244	- `catalog_test.go` — tool selection, naming, schema and annotation building.
245	- `adapter_test.go` — request construction and in-process execution (`adapter.go`), plus result normalization and error shaping (`result.go`).
246	- `validation_test.go` — argument validation against input schemas.
247	- `service_test.go` — the origin-header check, plus the end-to-end MCP protocol
248	  (`initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`) confirming object-shaped
249	  `structuredContent`.
250	
251	## Design notes
252	
253	- **Two-layer input validation.** `validateToolArguments` runs a hand-rolled
254	  structural check (`validateSchemaValue`) and then the `google/jsonschema-go`
255	  validator. The first yields friendly messages; the second is the
256	  spec-complete backstop.
257	- **Embedded vs. file load.** Production reads the spec from
258	  `proto.OpenAPIYAML()` (`loadMCPServiceOpenAPISpec`). The path-based
259	  `loadOpenAPISpec` in `openapi.go` exists for tests.
260	- **Tools only.** The server advertises no prompts or resources in this version.

## Search Results: GraphQL Schema Files

### Key Findings

**No GraphQL schema files exist in this repository.** The search for `.graphql` and `.gql` file extensions returned no results.

### Public API Structure

Instead of GraphQL, this repository uses **Protocol Buffers (protobuf) and OpenAPI** as the public API specification:

#### Primary API Schema Files

1. **OpenAPI Specification (Generated):**
   - `/bench/repo/proto/gen/openapi.yaml` (4,057 lines)
   - Auto-generated from proto definitions using `protoc-gen-openapi`
   - Embedded in the Go binary via `/bench/repo/proto/openapi_embed.go`

2. **Protocol Buffer Service Definitions:**
   - `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/ai_service.proto`
   - `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/attachment_service.proto`
   - `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/auth_service.proto`

   - `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/shortcut_service.proto`
   - `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/user_service.proto`

#### API Implementation Locations

- **Go API Handlers:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/`
- **MCP (Model Context Protocol) Service:** `/bench/repo/server/router/mcp/` (OpenAPI-driven, serves `/mcp` endpoint)
- **Generated TypeScript Types:** `/bench/repo/web/src/types/proto/`

#### Public API Documentation

- `/bench/repo/AGENTS.md` - "Add public API endpoints to `server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go`"
- `/bench/repo/server/router/mcp/README.md` - Comprehensive documentation of the OpenAPI-driven MCP service
- `/bench/repo/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-08-openapi-mcp-support-design.md` - OpenAPI MCP design specification
- `/bench/repo/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-08-openapi-mcp-support.md` - OpenAPI MCP planning document

### Architecture Overview

The repository implements a **single-source-of-truth API architecture**:
- Proto definitions (`proto/api/v1/*.proto`) define the service contracts
- `buf generate` produces OpenAPI YAML (`proto/gen/openapi.yaml`), Go bindings, and TypeScript types
- REST API handlers (`server/router/api/v1/`) implement the services
- MCP service (`server/router/mcp/`) derives tools directly from the OpenAPI spec and dispatches to the REST API
